raw_case_text:
A 20-year-old Hispanic male with no significant prior medical history presented to the emergency department with complaints of nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and diarrhea for 3 weeks. History was significant for high-risk sexual behaviors, anorexia, 10-pound weight loss, and low-grade fever. Physical examination revealed a cachectic male not in any distress. Heart rate was 104/min, blood pressure was 124/88 mm Hg, respiratory rate was 18/min, oxygen saturation of 95% on room air, and temperature was 98.3 F. Abdominal examination was significant for tenderness without visceromegaly. The remainder of the physical examination was unremarkable.
Laboratory studies showed a WBC count 8.2/microL, hemoglobin 11 g/dL, platelets 458,000/microL, and normal renal and liver function. Chest X-ray showed minimal right-sided pleural effusion. Computed tomography (CT) scan of chest and abdomen without contrast was obtained and showed bilateral pleural effusions, diffuse mesenteric lymphadenopathy, mesenteric edema, minimal ascites, diffuse ill-defined omental hyperdensities, and regional lymphadenopathy suspicious for carcinomatosis peritonei (Fig. 1).
Colonoscopy showed evidence of terminal ileitis along with submucosal nodular lesions (Fig. 2). Biopsies of ileal lesions did not reveal any malignancy but did show numerous CM spherules (Fig. 3). HIV screening test was positive. The patient was started on amphotericin B, 5 mg/kg intravenously. Serum CEA, CA 19-9, interferon gamma release assay, serum serotonin, and 24-hour urine 5-HIAA were normal. Serum CM antibody titer by complement fixation was 1: 2,048 (normal range <1: 2). Immunodiffusion assay revealed CM IgG level of 9.4 (normal range <0.9). HIV RNA level was 48,000 copies/mL, wild-type genotype, and no mutations. CD4 count was 102/microL. On hospital day 10, the patient developed shortness of breath and chest X-ray showed worsening pleural effusions. Thoracocentesis showed the fluid to be exudative with a white cell count of 1,018 (48% lymphocytes, 42% mesothelial cells). Pleural fluid cultures were negative for bacterial, mycobacterial, and fungal growth. On hospital day 17, a repeat CT of the abdomen showed improvement and the patient was clinically much better. Oral fluconazole 800 mg was started after completion of 2 weeks' therapy of amphotericin B. Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 160/800 mg one tablet daily was added for Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia prophylaxis. The patient was subsequently discharged. At 5 weeks' follow-up, the patient reported resolution of all his symptoms. Antiretroviral therapy was initiated. At 16 weeks' follow-up, serum CM titer by complement fixation decreased to 1: 256 and CD4 lymphocytes increased to 369/microL. Serum HIV RNA level was <20 copies/mL. The plan is to continue oral fluconazole for at least 1 year and lifelong antiretroviral therapy.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 20-year-old Hispanic male presented to the emergency department with a 3-week history of nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhea, anorexia, low-grade fever, and a 10-lb weight loss.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Over the 3 weeks prior to presentation, the patient developed persistent gastrointestinal symptoms (nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, watery diarrhea) accompanied by anorexia, low-grade fevers, and a 10-lb weight loss.
subjective.past_medical_history: No significant prior medical history; sexual history notable for high-risk sexual behaviors.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhea, anorexia, low-grade fever, and 10-lb weight loss; developed inpatient dyspnea on hospital day 10.

objective.physical_examination: Cachectic appearance, not in acute distress; heart rate 104/min, blood pressure 124/88 mmHg, respiratory rate 18/min, SpO2 95% on room air, and temperature 98.3 °F. Abdominal examination revealed diffuse tenderness without hepatosplenomegaly; remainder of the physical exam was normal.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission labs showed WBC 8.2 x 10^3/µL, hemoglobin 11 g/dL, platelets 458,000/µL, normal liver and renal function, and positive HIV screening test. Serum CEA, CA 19-9, IGRA, serum serotonin, and 24-hour urine 5-HIAA were normal. Serum Coccidioides immitis (CM) complement fixation antibody titer was markedly elevated at 1:2,048 (normal <1:2; declining to 1:256 at 16 weeks) and immunodiffusion IgG was 9.4 (normal <0.9). Chest X-ray showed a small right pleural effusion that progressed to bilateral effusions on day 10.
objective.advanced_workup: Baseline CD4+ T-cell count was 102 cells/µL (rising to 369 cells/µL at 16 weeks). Non-contrast chest and abdominal CT demonstrated bilateral pleural effusions, diffuse mesenteric and regional lymphadenopathy, mesenteric edema, minimal ascites, and diffuse omental caking/hyperdensities mimicking peritoneal carcinomatosis. Colonoscopy revealed terminal ileitis with submucosal nodular lesions; terminal ileal biopsy histopathology excluded malignancy and demonstrated numerous Coccidioides spherules. Day 10 thoracentesis yielded lymphocytic exudative pleural fluid (WBC 1,018/µL: 48% lymphocytes, 42% mesothelial cells) with negative cultures.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Disseminated abdominal, ileal, nodal, omental, and pleural coccidioidomycosis mimicking peritoneal carcinomatosis and unmasking newly diagnosed advanced HIV-1 infection (baseline plasma HIV-1 RNA 48,000 copies/mL with wild-type genotype and no resistance mutations; CD4+ count 102 cells/µL). Confirmed by terminal ileal biopsy showing Coccidioides spherules, serum complement fixation titer of 1:2,048, and CM IgG of 9.4. Treated with intravenous amphotericin B (5 mg/kg/day) for 2 weeks followed by long-term oral fluconazole (800 mg daily planned for >=1 year), daily oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (160/800 mg) for PCP prophylaxis, and initiation of antiretroviral therapy at week 5. By 16-week follow-up, the patient was completely asymptomatic with serum CM complement fixation titer reduced to 1:256, CD4+ count increased to 369 cells/µL, and plasma HIV-1 RNA suppressed to <20 copies/mL.
